description: A link set in running text, such as a sentence in an empty state or a help line. The link is a real <a href>, underlined at all times. A plain primary click is reported through navigate for a router, and every other activation stays the browser's.

content.description: The link text. Required, and guarded at runtime: a link with no text has no name, so an empty one, or one holding only spaces, throws.

href.description: Where the link goes. Required, and guarded at runtime after trimming: an <a> without an address is not a link and takes no focus.

external.description: Opens the address in a new tab. Arena writes target="_blank", adds noopener and noreferrer to rel, and says the locale's linkExternal word after the text without drawing it. The member is the one route to a new tab, and nothing is cancelled: a router cannot own a tab it did not open, so navigate does not fire.

download.description: Saves the address instead of navigating to it, under the name the browser chooses. Nothing is cancelled and navigate does not fire, because a router cannot own a download.

rel.description: Link types the consumer adds to rel, such as nofollow or ugc. Arena merges them with its own: it adds noopener whenever the link opens another browsing context, through external or a target that names one. Arena drops an opener token, so no list written here hands the new page this one.

target.description: A named browsing context the link opens in, such as a help window reused across links, or a keyword such as _top. _blank is not taken here: a new tab is external, so a _blank target is ignored and warned once. A target it writes other than _self cancels nothing and fires no navigate. The navigation happens in a context a router does not own.

navigate.description: The link was activated by the one activation a router owns, a primary click with no modifier, or Enter on the focused link. Arena has already cancelled the anchor's own navigation by the time the event fires. A modified click, a middle click and a context menu are the browser's and fire nothing, and so does a link that is external, a download or targeted elsewhere. No payload, because the consumer wrote this element and already holds what it is about.
